title: Genome-Wide Identification and Analysis of the MADS-Box Gene Family in Tectona grandis (Teak), a Member of the Lamiaceae Family.
authors: Alhindi, Tareq; Al-Hadid, Khaldoun J; Al-Abdallat, Ayed M
one_liner_zh: 该文对柚木MADS-box转录因子家族进行全基因组鉴定与进化分析，并用分子动力学模拟预测花四聚体结构稳定性，虽涉及TF-DNA互作较少，但蛋白复合物建模方法对TF-DNA研究有借鉴价值。
abstract: BACKGROUND: In plants, members of the MADS-box gene family encode transcription factors that regulate a wide range of developmental processes, including cell differentiation, organ identity, floral induction, and responses to environmental stimuli. Moreover, MADS-box genes play central roles in the well-known ABCDE model of floral development. Teak (Tectona grandis), a woody species belonging to the Lamiaceae family, is recognized for its medicinal and agricultural significance. The recent availability of a chromosome-level genome assembly for T. grandis has enabled the genome-wide identification of 87 MADS-box genes, which are distributed across 18 pseudo-chromosomes. METHODS: The amino acid sequences of these genes were compared with orthologous proteins from Arabidopsis thaliana, Sesamum indicum, and Amborella trichopoda to infer the phylogenetic relationships. The structures of key floral quartets in the MADS-box proteins were predicted, and the stability of these predicted tetramers were analyzed via molecular dynamics simulations. RESULTS: The phylogenetic analysis classified the genes into 33 Type I and 54 Type II MADS-box members, forming four major clades (MIKC(C), MIKC*, Malpha, and Mgamma), while the Mbeta-type clade was absent. A conserved motif analysis revealed that the Type II genes exhibited greater motif diversity than the Type I, suggesting that T. grandis Type II MADS-box genes possess more complex structures and potentially broader functions. The transcriptomic data from different tissues showed that the MIKC-type genes were particularly active during flower development. Although stable over the simulation time, the T. grandis AP3 ortholog had shorter I and K domains and had an odd mode of protein-protein interaction. CONCLUSION: Overall, the presented genome-wide analysis provides a comprehensive base for understanding the evolutionary diversification of the MADS-box gene family in T. grandis and identifies candidate genes for future structural and functional characterization.
abstract_zh: 背景：在植物中，MADS-box基因家族成员编码转录因子，调控广泛的发育过程，包括细胞分化、器官身份、花诱导以及对环境刺激的响应。此外，MADS-box基因在著名的花发育ABCDE模型中发挥核心作用。柚木（Tectona grandis）属于唇形科（Lamiaceae）的木本物种，因其药用和农业重要性而受到认可。近期获得的柚木染色体水平基因组组装使得全基因组范围内鉴定出87个MADS-box基因成为可能，这些基因分布在18条假染色体上。方法：将这些基因的氨基酸序列与拟南芥（Arabidopsis thaliana）、芝麻（Sesamum indicum）和互叶梅（Amborella trichopoda）的直系同源蛋白进行比较，以推断系统发育关系。预测了MADS-box蛋白中关键花四聚体的结构，并通过分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟分析了这些预测四聚体的稳定性。结果：系统发育分析将这些基因分为33个Type I和54个Type II MADS-box成员，形成四个主要分支（MIKC(C)、MIKC*、Malpha和Mgamma），而Mbeta型分支缺失。保守基序分析显示，Type II基因比Type I表现出更高的基序多样性，表明柚木Type II MADS-box基因具有更复杂的结构和潜在更广泛的功能。来自不同组织的转录组数据显示，MIKC型基因在花发育过程中特别活跃。尽管在模拟时间内稳定，柚木AP3直系同源物具有较短的I和K结构域，并表现出异常的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用模式。结论：总体而言，所呈现的全基因组分析为理解柚木MADS-box基因家族的进化多样化提供了全面基础，并鉴定了未来结构和功能表征的候选基因。
